This Week in Shortwave: FEBC Philippines Sets End Date

By Michael Smith (KM7FMJ) · November 16, 2026 · 4 min read

Another Christian broadcaster has set a date to leave shortwave: FEBC Philippines will switch off its transmitters on April 1, 2027. On the brighter side, a free browser app makes public KiwiSDRs easier to use, a listener crunched five weeks of pirate logs, and ShortwaveHQ gained DX filters, a closures tracker and Persian and Arabic sections.

Heard something this week? Send your catch to hqshortwaveradio@gmail.com and it may appear in next week's issue.

Top story: FEBC Philippines to end shortwave on April 1, 2027

FEBC Philippines has announced it will conclude shortwave broadcasting from its sites at Iba, Zambales and Bocaue, Bulacan, effective April 1, 2027. The decision was made by the FEBC International Executive Committee in March 2026, based on research with partner InterSearch showing that global shortwave listenership keeps falling, and all FEBC member fields agreed to phase shortwave out. The announcement does not list which frequencies or language services are affected.

Why it matters: Bocaue and Iba carry a large share of the religious programming heard across Asia on shortwave, and this follows WEWN's sign-off last month. Log FEBC while you can, and expect more open channels in the Asian evening hours next season. We'll add it to our shortwave closures tracker when the transmitters actually go quiet.

On the schedule tracker

A stable week: the daily EIBI updates brought no stations added, removed or moved. If you want something reliable tonight in North America, try Radio Romania International in English at 0100–0200 UTC on 7220 and 7325 kHz, Radio Habana Cuba at 0100–0200 UTC on 9710 kHz, or Voice of Turkey at 2300–2400 UTC on 5960 kHz. Band conditions

As of Nov 15 (12:43 UTC, NOAA SWPC): solar flux 124, sunspot number 121, K-index 0, A-index 2. Flux peaked at 132 mid-week, dipped to 116, and is climbing again. A K-index of 0 means a very quiet geomagnetic field: a good week for polar paths and for chasing weak signals on 60 m and 90 m after dark. In daylight, 25 m to 19 m are rated excellent, with 16 m and 13 m still good. Live conditions → · Grey line map →

News roundup

Skywave: KiwiSDRs in your browser. Skywave (skywavehf.com) is a free, ad-free web player for public KiwiSDR receivers. Press Listen and it picks the Kiwi with the best reported signal-to-noise on your frequency, falls back to the next one if it is full, scans mediumwave and 14 shortwave broadcast bands and labels the strongest signals from EiBi. It uses only one listener slot per Kiwi. Why it matters: it takes the guesswork out of choosing a remote receiver; just disconnect when you're done, since these are volunteer-run. More options on our Listen Online page.

Five weeks on the pirate band, by the numbers. Pete Jernakoff, K3KMS, used an AI assistant to collect North American pirate logs from HF Underground nightly for 37 days (Sept. 23 to Oct. 29). The result: 282 logs, about 85 station names on 41 frequencies, mostly in the 43 m band (6850–6999 kHz). Weekends averaged 11.4 logs a day against 6.2 on weekdays, 68% fell between 2200 and 0359 UTC, and 0000–0059 UTC was the busiest hour. USB carried 68% of logs. Most-logged: Liquid Radio, Route 66 Radio, WTPK and Bandaid Radio. Why it matters: if you want to hear pirates, tune 43 m on a weekend evening around 0000 UTC.

Hobby broadcasters. RNEI aired an hour-long special on Irish singer-songwriter Emma O'Reilly on Sunday (Nov 15) at 1900 UTC on 1467 and 6195 kHz, and Texas Radio Shortwave has posted its December 2026 schedule (see trswradio.com).

Heard on the air. Carlos Latuff shared another illustrated log and recording of Reach Beyond Australia’s Japanese service (Nov 12), a programme on Kanreki, Japan's 60th-birthday tradition.

Your turn

FEBC and EWTN both cited falling listenership. If you were running a broadcaster, would you keep a shortwave budget? Tell us in the HQ Shortwave Radio Listeners group on Facebook, or email us.

Sources: FEBC Philippines, SWLing Post (FEBC, Skywave), Skywave, SWLing Post (K3KMS pirate study), SWLing Post (RNEI), SWLing Post (Texas Radio Shortwave), SWLing Post (Carlos Latuff), NOAA SWPC, EIBI.
